svg.title: Bi-encoder: the query and the document never meet
svg.desc: A hand-drawn whiteboard split down the middle. On the left a bi-encoder passes the query and the chunk through two copies of the same encoder that are separated by a red dashed line labelled THEY NEVER MEET, each producing a vector strip which meet only at a cosine circle giving 0.71, with a note that the document side is computed once at ingest - 47,300 chunks in 33 minutes - and is free at query time. On the right a cross-encoder takes one concatenated query-SEP-chunk input through a single model to 0.83, annotated in red that nothing can be precomputed and scoring the full corpus would take 43 seconds. Below, a scatter of chunk points around a query cross inside a dashed top-10 ring with two shaded as relevant, and four bars showing gte-large is 3.9 times slower for 0.005 more recall.
svg.text: Bi-encoder: the query and the document never meet
query time this side is FREE.
that is why it re-ranks. It can never retrieve.
dashed ring = top-10. Only 2 are relevant.
